doc.title: Bobby Shew interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 1, 2020

title: What a studio call involves; the Universal contractor Sandy DeCrescent
summary: Shew explains doubles pay and mutes, and tells how a secretary became the Universal contractor.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: I wonder if you could get real specific for me, because I’ve been curious about — you show up, first of all you get a call from the contractor, and they tell you the studio and the time. Do you get any other information like make sure you have your mutes? Bring your flugelhorn? Or are you just expected to know that part of it?
Part of it you’re expected to always have your mutes with you.

A flugelhorn, not necessarily, or a piccolo trumpet, or anything they’re called doubles as you know, if the contractor calls you and says, “Bring a flugelhorn, they have to pay you for it whether you play it or not.” Okay? So if the call is out for the doubles, you know, when I was working at Universal there was a lady there by the name of Sandy DeCrescent who was not a musician at all, she was the secretary to the guy that was the contractor and he committed suicide. And so the union people, mostly the string players and French horn players, you know typically, they thought let’s vote to have Sandy be the contractor. See you have to be a musician in the musicians’ union to be a contractor. And she wasn’t. She was a secretary. But they thought well let’s make her a musician. So they made her a maraca player. And they paid for her to join thinking that because they were on the list from the previous contractor that she would call them. Well she didn’t. She started calling different people. And it all backfired on them. But Sandy became the Universal Studios contractor for years. And she was a pain in the ass. She didn’t know nothing. So I got calls from her and told me to remind me to bring my flute and clarinet. She didn’t know. And I’d go there and I’d say, you know you used to fill out the W9 and
all that and you think like should I put flute and clarinet on there and make her pay for this you know? And I was like no, I’m not going to do it.
